solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Young elephant is mostly placid with female

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all of the word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: placid means calm

explanation.surface: A baby elephant is described as being, for the most part, a calm female.
explanation.definitionFit: The offspring of an elephant, like that of a cow or whale, is called by the same name as a young bovine.

clue.text: Part of great road taken over for major artery

indicators.note: taken over, in a down clue, means the hidden letters are turned upside down, read bottom to top
part of says the letters sit inside the words great road, running across the gap between them

explanation.surface: A stretch of a major road has been taken over to serve as a main traffic artery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part of' hides ATROA in greATROAd; 'taken over' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: The body's main artery carries blood from the heart; 'major artery' is a straight description.

clue.text: Begin to make sense of reduction in best fabric

parts.note: a fall is a drop or reduction, as in a fall in prices
top means best, as in the top student
lace is a delicate openwork fabric

explanation.surface: Someone finally understands why the finest cloth has been marked down.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes puzzling facts suddenly fitting together and becoming clear.

clue.text: Naval colleague met seas running around head in Morocco

indicators.note: around means the rearranged letters wrap round the next piece
running suggests the letters of met seas moving about into a new order
head in means the first letter of the word Morocco

explanation.surface: A sailor met high seas on a voyage round the coast near Morocco.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running' rearranges the seven letters into two words split apart, and 'around' wraps them round the Morocco initial.
explanation.definitionFit: A shipmate who shares meals with you in the same mess on a warship is a fellow sailor.

clue.text: Bavarian capital not allowing one to eat noisily

indicators.note: not allowing means the following piece is shut out of the city's name

parts.note: Munich is the capital of the German state of Bavaria
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A German city bans a visitor from chomping loudly.
explanation.definitionFit: To chomp food audibly is a synonym; crunching or chewing with relish.

clue.text: Slug eating every bulb

indicators.note: eating means one word takes the other into its middle

parts.note: a slug is a shot, a gulp of spirits or a bullet
every means all

explanation.surface: A garden slug is munching through every bulb in the bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slug' looks like the garden pest but means a drink or a bullet.
explanation.definitionFit: This small onion-like vegetable grows as a bulb, so it is an example of one.

clue.text: Get wrong man with sudden stir breaking out

indicators.note: breaking out suggests the letters burst free of their order and regroup

explanation.surface: Someone misreads a man who suddenly makes a commotion during a prison break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking out' rearranges MAN and SUDDENSTIR together.
explanation.definitionFit: To fail to grasp something correctly is to have the wrong idea about it.

clue.text: Quality gold for betrayer

parts.note: a trait is a quality or characteristic
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: Someone sold out for a valuable quality or for gold.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: one who betrays a cause or country is a turncoat.

clue.text: Ask Iran possibly to absorb large island state

indicators.note: to absorb means the rearranged letters take the next piece inside them
possibly suggests the letters of Ask Iran might be arranged differently

explanation.surface: A diplomat suggests asking Iran to take in a big island nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges ASKIRAN to SRIANKA; 'to absorb' takes in L.
explanation.definitionFit: The country is an island nation south of India, formerly Ceylon.

clue.text: Good man has certainly to remain steady

parts.note: ST, short for saint, is the crossword good man
ay, an old form of aye, means yes or certainly

explanation.surface: A virtuous man surely intends to stand firm.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep still or not budge from one's position is to stop where one is and not move.

clue.text: Proscribe party seizing Northern Ireland

indicators.note: seizing means the party word grabs the next piece and holds it inside

parts.note: a bash is a party

explanation.surface: A political party is outlawed for taking control of Northern Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'party' is the noun for a celebration, not a political group.
explanation.definitionFit: To prohibit or exile someone is to proscribe them; outlaw is a shared sense.

clue.text: Public transport is mostly out of action?

indicators.note: mostly means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: bust means broken, out of action

explanation.surface: A grumble that the buses and trains are usually broken down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims BUST to its first three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A road vehicle carrying passengers on a fixed route is the commonest example of public transport.

clue.text: Linear extent not getting the height, initially?

definitions.text: Linear extent not getting the height, initially?

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of each of the preceding six words

explanation.surface: A definition of measurement in one direction, without counting how tall a thing is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes the first letter of every word before it; the whole clue also defines the answer, since a linear extent ignores height.
explanation.definitionFit: This measurement is one dimension, distinct from height and width, so the whole clue describes it.

clue.text: Small London gallery frequently has core of real modernity

parts.note: the Tate is a London art gallery
oft is an old word for often, frequently
the heart of something is its core

explanation.surface: A small London gallery often displays the essence of genuinely modern work.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tate is a group of art galleries in London. 'has' joins OFT to HEART; 'core' is the synonym, not a pick from 'real'.
explanation.definitionFit: Used adjectivally the phrase describes the latest, most advanced technology, so it means genuinely up to date.

clue.text: Queen going by rail to see the lie of the land

indicators.note: going by means the queen travels inside the train

parts.note: a train is rail transport
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword queen

explanation.surface: The monarch takes the royal train to survey the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the usual crossword queen.
explanation.definitionFit: The physical features and contours of a stretch of ground are its layout or landscape.

clue.text: Inaccurate actors will be ostracised

parts.note: out means wrong or inaccurate, as in a calculation being out
the cast is the set of actors in a play

explanation.surface: Performers who get their lines wrong will be shunned by the company.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an adjective, the word describes someone rejected and shunned by society.

clue.text: Time to set up for a little drink

indicators.note: set up, in a down clue, means the word to is written bottom to top

explanation.surface: It is time to arrange a small drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A small measure of spirits, such as a dram of whisky, is a little drink.

clue.text: One tramp unfortunately a source of odour?

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests the letters have come to a bad end and been jumbled

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: An unlucky vagrant who smells rather strongly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' rearranges I and TRAMP together. The question mark marks a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: The underarm is a well-known site of body sweat and smell, so it is one example of a smelly spot.

clue.text: Rock made of barium and sodium chloride

parts.note: Ba is the chemical symbol for barium
sodium chloride is common salt

explanation.surface: A chemistry claim that a rock is composed of barium and table salt.
explanation.definitionFit: This dark volcanic stone is a type of igneous rock.

clue.text: Anger about grand nonsense

indicators.note: about means the anger word goes round the next piece

parts.note: bile means anger or bitterness
G is short for grand, a thousand pounds or dollars

explanation.surface: Someone rages about pompous rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for rubbish talk, from the dirty water in a ship's hull.

clue.text: Certain place swarming grasshopper is finally eradicated

indicators.note: finally eradicated means the last letter of the insect is wiped out

parts.note: a locust is a grasshopper that forms huge swarms

explanation.surface: A plague of insects has at last been wiped out from a particular spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally eradicated' removes the final T of LOCUST.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for place, used in mathematics and science for a particular position or site.

clue.text: Long history of silver being found in South Africa

indicators.note: being found in means the silver sits inside the country's abbreviation

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A long tale of silver being found in South Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: A lengthy family or historical chronicle, like the Norse prose tales, is an epic story.

clue.text: Union has no beginning in casual relationship

indicators.note: has no beginning means the first letter is taken off

parts.note: a dalliance is a casual love affair

explanation.surface: A marriage that began as nothing more than a fling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has no beginning' drops the first letter of DALLIANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: A pact or coalition joining parties together is a union of allies.

clue.text: Peacekeepers resolve trouble

parts.note: the UN, United Nations, provides peacekeeping forces
to settle a dispute is to resolve it

explanation.surface: United Nations troops are sent to sort out a conflict.
explanation.definitionFit: To disturb or upset someone is a synonym, making them anxious.

clue.text: Fly with blue back and head of hideousness

indicators.note: back means the word is read in reverse

parts.note: blue means sad, low in spirits

indicators.note: head of means the first letter of the word hideousness

explanation.surface: An insect described as having a blue back and an ugly head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns SAD into DAS. 'Fly' looks like the insect but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To rush or hurry somewhere is a verb synonym, as in having to run off quickly.
